title: Learning to GUIDE the Group: Self-Learning LLM Facilitation Across Multi-Party Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.16231v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large language models are increasingly adopted as multi-party communication facilitators, there is a growing demand for agents capable of balancing diverse group dynamics across contexts. However, existing LLM facilitators are often fine-tuned for task-specific objectives; generalized LLM-based facilitation methods that can adapt to different types of tasks and diverse group dynamics are underdeveloped. To address this gap, we present GUIDE (Generalized Unified Intervention for Dynamic Exchanges, a framework for developing generalized LLM-based facilitators across different multi-party contexts. GUIDE evaluates facilitation across both objective task outcomes and subjective metrics, including psychological safety and perceived friction. Within this framework, we study whether LLMs can self-learn generalized facilitation strategy offline to real-time interventions. translated_title: 学会引导群体：面向多方任务的自学习大语言模型协调方法
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型被越来越多地用作多方沟通的协调者，人们日益需要能够在不同情境下平衡多样化群体动态的智能体。然而，现有的LLM协调器通常针对特定任务目标进行微调，能够适应不同类型任务和多样群体动态的通用LLM协调方法仍不完善。为弥补这一空白，我们提出了GUIDE（Generalized Unified Intervention for Dynamic Exchanges，动态交流的通用统一干预），一个用于开发跨不同多方情境的通用LLM协调器的框架。GUIDE从客观任务结果和主观指标（包括心理安全感和感知摩擦）两方面评估协调效果。在该框架内，我们研究LLM能否离线自学习通用的协调策略并将其应用于实时干预。我们首先收集由任务特定目标引导的多方人类互动……
tldr: 该论文提出了GUIDE框架，通过同时评估客观任务结果与心理安全感等主观指标，研究LLM能否离线自学习出可跨多种多方任务情境泛化的通用协调策略。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces GUIDE, a framework that evaluates LLM facilitation through both objective task outcomes and subjective metrics (e.g., psychological safety), and investigates whether LLMs can self-learn generalized facilitation strategies that transfer across diverse multi-party tasks.
